chunks: From him, from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who advances payment for sheep, specifying two-year-olds and one-year-olds, and other such categories, for a fixed term. He said: 'There is no harm. If the one who owes the sheep is unable to pay all that he owes, the owner of the sheep takes half of them, or a third, or two-thirds, and takes the principal value of the remaining sheep in dirhams. They take according to their conditions and do not take more than their conditions.' He said: 'And the same applies to wool, just as it applies to wheat, barley, saffron, and sheep.'

key_terms.يُسْلِفُ: To advance payment or give a loan in advance

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for advance payment contracts (salam) for livestock if the seller cannot deliver all the specified animals?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of *bay' al-salam* (advance payment sale) in Shia jurisprudence, specifically addressing the liquidation of livestock debts where the debtor lacks sufficient animals. It establishes that creditors may take a proportional share of the remaining livestock and convert the monetary value of the deficit into cash, provided they adhere strictly to the agreed terms without excess. The extension of this ruling to other commodities like wheat, barley, and saffron underscores the principle of uniformity in commercial contracts across diverse goods.
